issues.legal_issue: A High Court hearing a civil revision may examine the underlying record for compliance with safeguards for a minor even when the procedural defect was not raised by a party.
material_facts: The revision challenged the refusal to condone delay in applying to set aside an ex parte decree.
A minor was a defendant, and an application to appoint a guardian for the minor had been filed with the suit.
The trial court closed the guardian-appointment application after noting that a vakalat had been filed, without properly appointing a guardian under the applicable procedure.
The High Court summoned the original record and identified the failure to appoint a guardian.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was entitled to examine the original record and determine whether a guardian had been properly appointed, notwithstanding the absence of a specific contention on that point.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the High Court may call for and examine the record in a revision. Order XXXII, Rule 3, as amended for courts subject to the Madras High Court, prescribes rigorous safeguards for appointing a guardian for a minor defendant. Sections 121 and 122 of the Code provide for the effect of First Schedule rules and the High Courts' power to alter them. The High Court may examine compliance with such safeguards, particularly where a person under disability is concerned.

rule.if: revision_from_delay_refusal and minor_is_defendant and guardian_appointment_is_in_doubt and record_shows_no_proper_appointment

predicates.revision_from_delay_refusal: A party seeks revision of an order refusing to condone delay in applying to set aside an ex parte decree.
predicates.minor_is_defendant: A minor is a defendant in the underlying civil suit.
predicates.guardian_appointment_is_in_doubt: The circumstances give the reviewing court reason to doubt whether a guardian was properly appointed for the minor.
predicates.record_shows_no_proper_appointment: The underlying court record shows that no guardian was appointed in the manner required for the minor's representation.

issues.definition: When a revision concerns refusal to condone delay, a minor is a defendant, and the record raises doubt about proper guardian appointment, the High Court may examine that appointment.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court may use its supervisory jurisdiction to set aside an ex parte decree while hearing a revision arising from refusal to condone delay in seeking to set it aside.
material_facts: The defendants sought condonation of substantial delay in applying to set aside an ex parte decree, and the trial court refused their application.
In revision, the High Court found that a minor defendant had not been represented by a guardian appointed in accordance with the applicable procedure.
The High Court set aside the decree without deciding whether there was sufficient cause for the delay.
The minor was found to have suffered prejudice.
issues.conclusion: The High Court did not exceed its jurisdiction by invoking its supervisory power to set aside the ex parte decree in the revision proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: Article 227 of the Constitution confers supervisory jurisdiction that is additional to and wider than the revisional jurisdiction under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Surya Dev Rai v. Ram Chander Rai and Others was overruled by Radhey Shyam v. Chhabi Nath and Others on the availability of Article 226 relief, but Radhey Shyam distinguished the jurisdiction under Article 227. The failure to appoint a guardian under Order XXXII, Rule 3, coupled with the finding of prejudice to the minor, supported intervention; the Court did not decide whether such a decree is automatically a nullity in every case.

predicates.revision_from_delay_refusal: A party seeks revision of an order refusing to condone delay in applying to set aside an ex parte decree.
predicates.minor_lacked_proper_guardian: A minor defendant was not represented by a guardian appointed in accordance with the applicable procedure.
predicates.minor_suffered_prejudice: The minor was prejudiced by the failure to provide proper representation in the suit.

issues.definition: When a revision concerns refusal to condone delay and the minor defendant lacked a properly appointed guardian and suffered prejudice, the High Court may set aside the ex parte decree.

issues.legal_issue: Where an ex parte decree is treated as a nullity because a minor defendant lacked a properly appointed guardian, the decree need not be set aside only as against the minor.
material_facts: The ex parte decree was entered in a suit involving several defendants, including a minor.
The minor had not been represented by a guardian properly appointed under the applicable procedure, and the minor was found to have been prejudiced.
The challenge was made that the decree should have been set aside only as against the minor.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the contention that relief had to be limited to the minor, because the decree was treated as a nullity in law.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXXII, Rule 3, as applicable to the proceedings, requires proper appointment of a guardian for a minor defendant. Order XXXII, Rule 3-A addresses prejudice where a next friend or guardian has an interest adverse to the minor; the Court noted that this case did not fall within that category and did not decide whether every decree passed without proper appointment is ipso facto a nullity. Given the finding of prejudice and the treatment of this decree as a nullity, the Court rejected limiting the setting aside to the minor alone.

rule.if: civil_suit_includes_minor_defendant and minor_lacked_proper_guardian and minor_suffered_prejudice and decree_was_treated_as_nullity

predicates.civil_suit_includes_minor_defendant: The civil suit includes a minor as a defendant alongside other parties.
predicates.minor_lacked_proper_guardian: A minor defendant was not represented by a guardian appointed in accordance with the applicable procedure.
predicates.minor_suffered_prejudice: The minor was prejudiced by the failure to provide proper representation in the suit.
predicates.decree_was_treated_as_nullity: The decree was treated as a nullity because of the defect in the minor's representation.

issues.definition: When a suit includes a minor defendant who lacked a properly appointed guardian and suffered prejudice, and the decree is treated as a nullity, the entire decree may be set aside.
